passages.title: Three-dimensional Euclidean space
passages.quote: `Breakdown.Space`: The paper’s physical and similarity spaces are represented by Euclidean three-vectors with the usual inner-product norm. This fixed dimension is used in the drift integration by parts as well as in the Navier–Stokes operators.

passages.title: Three-dimensional Euclidean space
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.Space` (1): Fin 3 has exactly three coordinates; this is neither a variable-dimensional nor an empty ambient space.

passages.title: Three-dimensional Euclidean space
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.Space`, lines 10-10: Fix the ambient physical space to R³.

passages.title: Coordinate unit vectors
passages.quote: `Breakdown.unitVector`: These are the three standard basis vectors used to write the divergence, Laplacian and gradient of (1.1). Coordinates are numbered 0, 1 and 2 in Lean.

passages.title: Coordinate unit vectors
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.unitVector` (1): Every basis vector has norm one, so these coordinate sums cannot collapse through an empty or zero basis.

passages.title: Coordinate unit vectors
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.unitVector`, lines 12-12: These are the three standard basis vectors used to write the divergence, Laplacian and gradient of (1.1).

passages.title: Divergence
passages.quote: `Breakdown.divergenceAt`: This is the trace of the spatial derivative, representing div u in (1.1) and div W in (1.2). The derivative is stored as a continuous linear map.

passages.title: Divergence
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.divergenceAt` (1): Mathlib’s fderiv is total and is zero when differentiability fails; the smooth-solution and smooth-profile hypotheses supply differentiability where this operator is used.

passages.title: Divergence
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.divergenceAt`, lines 14-15: This is the trace of the spatial derivative, representing div u in (1.1) and div W in (1.2).

passages.title: Laplacian
passages.quote: `Breakdown.sumSecondPartialsAt`: The sum of the three diagonal second directional derivatives represents the vector Laplacian in (1.1). It uses the iterated Fréchet derivative rather than a componentwise array of scalar second derivatives.

passages.title: Laplacian
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.sumSecondPartialsAt` (1): The derivative expression is meaningful as the classical Laplacian under the surrounding smoothness hypotheses; it does not assert differentiability by itself.

passages.title: Laplacian
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.sumSecondPartialsAt`, lines 17-18: The sum of the three diagonal second directional derivatives represents the vector Laplacian in (1.1).

passages.title: Pressure gradient
passages.quote: `Breakdown.gradientAt`: This reconstructs the vector ∇p from the three coordinate derivatives of the scalar pressure. Only the gradient enters the equation, so adding a function of time to p does not change this term.

passages.title: Pressure gradient
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.gradientAt` (1): The raw fderiv operation is total; smooth_pressure or the profile’s smooth-pressure clause supplies the needed regularity.

passages.title: Pressure gradient
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.gradientAt`, lines 20-21: This reconstructs the vector ∇p from the three coordinate derivatives of the scalar pressure.

passages.title: Nonlinear transport
passages.quote: `Breakdown.advectionAt`: Applying the spatial derivative of v to v itself gives the paper’s (v·∇)v. This order of application fixes the convection convention used throughout the certificate files.

passages.title: Nonlinear transport
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.advectionAt` (1): The operation does not carry a differentiability proof; the classical and weak interfaces provide separate regularity contracts.

passages.title: Nonlinear transport
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.advectionAt`, lines 23-24: Applying the spatial derivative of v to v itself gives the paper’s (v·∇)v.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution`: This is the global solution class used in the formal nonexistence conclusions, with viscosity ν and initial velocity u₀. Joint smoothness is required on the closed nonnegative-time half-space; the PDE and incompressibility are imposed at positive times.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution` (1): ContDiffOn controls the initial trace and prevents a jump at time zero.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution` (2): For t>0 the regularity domain contains a neighbourhood, so deriv, fderiv and iteratedFDeriv are actual derivatives there.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution` (3): Values at negative times are outside the regularity and PDE requirements.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution` (4): Periodicity and the energy restriction are added by the endpoint predicates, rather than by this structure.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Field `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution.smooth_velocity`: The velocity is jointly smooth in time and space up to t=0.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Field `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution.smooth_pressure`: The pressure is jointly smooth in time and space up to t=0.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Field `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution.initial`: The velocity at t=0 equals the prescribed datum u₀ at every point.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Field `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution.momentum`: The unforced momentum equation holds at every positive time, with viscosity ν.

passages.title: Global smooth solution
passages.quote: Field `Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution.incompressible`: The velocity has zero divergence at every positive time.

passages.title: Breakdown on the whole space
passages.quote: `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace`: For each positive viscosity, this asks for smooth compactly supported solenoidal data admitting no global smooth solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy. It records a nonexistence endpoint and leaves the rate and profile convergence in Theorem 1.1 outside the conclusion.

passages.title: Breakdown on the whole space
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace` (1): The datum may depend on ν: the quantifier order is for every ν>0, there exists u₀.

passages.title: Breakdown on the whole space
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace` (2): The energy bound C is inside the forbidden solution existential; no fixed choice of a negative C can remove legitimate solutions.

passages.title: Breakdown on the whole space
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace` (3): The energy is an ENNReal lintegral bounded by finite ENNReal.ofReal C; no toReal conversion can turn infinite energy into zero.

passages.title: Breakdown on the whole space
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace`, lines 36-37: For each positive viscosity choose smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data.

passages.title: Breakdown on the whole space
passages.quote: Clause 2 of `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace`, lines 38-39: Exclude every global smooth solution for which one finite energy bound works at all nonnegative times.

passages.title: Breakdown on the torus
passages.quote: `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus`: For each positive viscosity, this asks for smooth solenoidal data of period one in each spatial coordinate admitting no global smooth solution with periodic velocity. The pressure remains unrestricted by periodicity, making the excluded class larger than the periodic-pressure class in the paper.

passages.title: Breakdown on the torus
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus` (1): The torus is encoded by periodic functions on R³, rather than by a quotient type.

passages.title: Breakdown on the torus
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus` (2): The existential pressure may be any smooth pressure; periodicity is imposed only on u₀ and u.

passages.title: Breakdown on the torus
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus` (3): There is no whole-space energy condition here.

passages.title: Breakdown on the torus
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus`, lines 42-43: For each positive viscosity choose smooth divergence-free data with period one along every coordinate.

passages.title: Breakdown on the torus
passages.quote: Clause 2 of `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus`, lines 44-45: Exclude all global smooth solutions whose velocity retains the periods, regardless of pressure periodicity.

passages.title: Self-similar equation residual
passages.quote: `Breakdown.SimilarityResidual`: This is the left-hand side of the velocity equation in (1.2), before setting it to zero. Its time variable is the similarity time s, so it contains no reciprocal-period factor.

passages.title: Self-similar equation residual
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.SimilarityResidual` (1): The classical derivative operations require the smoothness supplied by PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists.

passages.title: Self-similar equation residual
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.SimilarityResidual`, lines 48-49: Assemble time differentiation, dilation drift, diffusion, convection and pressure gradient in similarity variables.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`: A nonzero smooth pair (W,q) solves the self-similar equation and returns after a positive period P up to an orthogonal spatial transformation. The written premise includes second-derivative decay and pressure-gradient decay in addition to the two bounds displayed in (1.3).

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (1): R is a linear isometric equivalence, so its inverse is genuine; reflections are allowed.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (2): The nonzero clause is pointwise, and smoothness prevents a null-set modification of zero from satisfying it.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (3): A single finite real C controls all times and all spatial points.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (4): Remark 1.2 supplies the higher velocity estimate by analysis; the pressure-gradient bound is an additional written formal requirement with no separate bound in (1.3).

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 52-55: Choose smooth velocity and pressure, an orthogonal transformation and a strictly positive period.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 2 of `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 56-57: Require the self-similar equation and incompressibility at every time and point.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 3 of `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 58-58: Advance by one period and apply the spatial isometry to the field and its argument.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 4 of `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 59-59: Require a point at which the smooth velocity is nonzero.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 5 of `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 60-60: Control spatial derivatives of orders zero, one and two by the corresponding inverse powers of 1+|y|.

passages.title: Smooth recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 6 of `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 61-61: Require inverse-cubic decay of the pressure gradient.

passages.title: Compactly supported scalar test
passages.quote: `Breakdown.IsTestFunction`: This supplies the scalar C∞ compactly supported test functions used to express weak spatial derivatives. Such tests make integration by parts local in the spatial variable.

passages.title: Compactly supported scalar test
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsTestFunction` (1): A test is compactly supported in space; time is absent from this predicate.

passages.title: Compactly supported scalar test
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.IsTestFunction`, lines 63-63: This supplies the scalar C∞ compactly supported test functions used to express weak spatial derivatives.

passages.title: Weak spatial gradient
passages.quote: `Breakdown.IsWeakGradient`: This represents G=∇f by coordinate integration by parts against every smooth compactly supported scalar test. Both f and G must be locally integrable, so the derivative identity is a distributional statement with meaningful local pairings.

passages.title: Weak spatial gradient
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsWeakGradient` (1): The derivative is supplied as data and constrained by the test identity; fderiv f is not used.

passages.title: Weak spatial gradient
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsWeakGradient` (2): Mathlib’s Bochner integral is total, but local integrability and compact test support guard these particular integrals.

passages.title: Weak spatial gradient
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.IsWeakGradient`, lines 66-66: Require local integrability of both the field and its supplied gradient.

passages.title: Weak spatial gradient
passages.quote: Clause 2 of `Breakdown.IsWeakGradient`, lines 67-68: Test each coordinate derivative against every scalar smooth compactly supported function.

passages.title: Solenoidal space-time test
passages.quote: `Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestField`: These are the smooth compactly supported vector tests that remove pressure from the weak equation. Their divergence vanishes for every time and spatial point.

passages.title: Solenoidal space-time test
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestField` (1): Support is compact in the joint time-space variable; these tests are not required to be time-periodic.

passages.title: Solenoidal space-time test
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestField`, lines 71-72: Require joint smoothness, joint compact support and spatial divergence zero.

passages.title: Weak self-similar equation
passages.quote: `Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand`: This is the residual paired with a divergence-free test after moving time, drift, diffusion and convection derivatives onto that test. In three dimensions the half-velocity term and the integrated dilation drift combine to give the displayed negative unit coefficient on W·φ.

passages.title: Weak self-similar equation
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand` (1): The test’s derivatives are classical; W enters without a time derivative, and G supplies its weak spatial gradient.

passages.title: Weak self-similar equation
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand` (2): The pressure term vanishes against the divergence-free tests.

passages.title: Weak self-similar equation
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand` (3): WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists separately requires this complete signed integrand to be Integrable before setting its integral to zero.

passages.title: Weak self-similar equation
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand`, lines 76-78: Time integration by parts and the three-dimensional drift produce the negative time-test term, negative W·φ, and negative half radial-test term.

passages.title: Weak self-similar equation
passages.quote: Clause 2 of `Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand`, lines 79-79: Diffusion contributes the pairing of the weak gradient with the test gradient.

passages.title: Weak self-similar equation
passages.quote: Clause 3 of `Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand`, lines 80-80: Incompressibility moves the nonlinear transport derivative onto the test.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`: This is the explicit weak-profile interface used between the certificate construction and breakdown: recurrent velocity, supplied weak derivatives, uniform L⁶ and gradient-L² bounds, and the pressure-free distributional equation. Its quantifiers are more detailed than the continuous-X hypothesis in Proposition 7.11.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (1): The same finite real C bounds the sixth-power velocity integral and squared operator-norm gradient integral for every time.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (2): The gradient in this predicate uses the norm on continuous linear maps; the certificate’s matSq is the Frobenius square, an equivalent finite-dimensional norm.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (3): The second weak derivative is required for almost every time, whereas the first weak gradient and its spatial-a.e. divergence statement are required for every time.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (4): The final nontriviality clause is on product almost-everywhere equivalence classes and rejects null-set spikes.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` (5): The signed weak residual must be integrable; equality of a totalized integral to zero alone would not be the stated requirement.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 83-85: Choose the velocity, two supplied spatial derivative fields, a positive period and an isometry.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 2 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 86-88: Require joint almost-everywhere strong measurability for the velocity and both derivative fields.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 3 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 89-89: Require the velocity recurrence pointwise in time and space.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 4 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 90-92: The first derivative identity holds for every time; the second derivative identity holds for almost every time.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 5 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 93-93: At every time the supplied gradient has trace zero almost everywhere in space.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 6 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 94-95: One finite bound controls the velocity’s sixth-power integral and the gradient’s squared integral at every time.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 7 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 96-96: Require a finite squared second-derivative integral over one positive period.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 8 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 97-98: For every solenoidal test, require the weak residual to be integrable and its integral to vanish.

passages.title: Weak recurrent profile exists
passages.quote: Clause 9 of `Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileExists`, lines 99-99: Exclude velocity fields that vanish almost everywhere on space-time.

passages.title: Profile gives whole-space breakdown
passages.quote: `Breakdown.breakdown_on_space`: The exported implication sends a smooth recurrent profile to the whole-space nonexistence endpoint. The readable theorem contains a proof placeholder; Solution.lean supplies the implementation from the library.

passages.title: Profile gives whole-space breakdown
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.breakdown_on_space` (1): The profile remains an assumption; this theorem does not produce a numerical profile or validate a certificate.

passages.title: Profile gives whole-space breakdown
passages.quote: Comparison for `Breakdown.breakdown_on_space`: The written profile premise includes extra decay bounds, and the conclusion retains nonexistence for every positive viscosity while omitting the constructed trajectory, rate and convergence in Theorem 1.1. Relating the paper and formal endpoints uses the analytic bridges described in the authors’ README.

passages.title: Profile gives whole-space breakdown
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.breakdown_on_space`, lines 101-101: The readable implication has an explicit hypothesis and endpoint; its proof is supplied separately in Solution.lean.

passages.title: Profile gives torus breakdown
passages.quote: `Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus`: The exported implication sends a smooth recurrent profile to the periodic-velocity nonexistence endpoint. Its implementation also handles the pressure normalization needed to exclude global solutions whose pressure was not assumed periodic.

passages.title: Profile gives torus breakdown
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus` (1): The conclusion has neither an explicit blow-up time nor a rate or local convergence estimate.

passages.title: Profile gives torus breakdown
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus` (2): The theorem shown here is a stub, with the proof exposed separately by Solution.lean.

passages.title: Profile gives torus breakdown
passages.quote: Comparison for `Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus`: The formal conclusion excludes a larger pressure class than the paper’s periodic-pressure formulation and omits the trajectory, rate and convergence of (1.7). The hypothesis also writes additional profile decay bounds, so a single unqualified stronger/weaker label would hide changes in both directions.

passages.title: Profile gives torus breakdown
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus`, lines 104-104: The readable implication has an explicit hypothesis and endpoint; its proof is supplied separately in Solution.lean.

passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.breakdown_on_space_of_weak` (1): The weak hypothesis includes actual integrability and product-a.e. nontriviality; a pointwise spike in a zero equivalence class is excluded.

passages.title: Weak profile gives breakdown

passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.breakdown_on_space_of_weak`, lines 107-107: The readable implication has an explicit hypothesis and endpoint; its proof is supplied separately in Solution.lean.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.Symmetry`: A symmetry pairs an orthogonal transformation R with a shift θ₀ in normalized period-one time. The set Γ may be empty and is not required to be supplied as a group.

passages.title: Space-time symmetry

passages.title: Squared gradient matrix norm
passages.quote: `Breakdown.matSq`: Summing the squared lengths of the three coordinate directional derivatives gives the Frobenius square used for |∇v|² in Section 7. This differs from the operator-norm notation used by the weak-profile endpoint, although the two norms are equivalent in dimension three.

passages.title: Squared gradient matrix norm
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.matSq` (1): The paper writes (∇v)ⱼₖ=∂ⱼvₖ; in Lean this component is (G(eⱼ))ₖ, giving the same scalar norm despite the different storage convention.

passages.title: Squared gradient matrix norm
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.matSq`, lines 12-12: Summing the squared lengths of the three coordinate directional derivatives gives the Frobenius square used for |∇v|² in Section 7.

passages.title: Gradient matrix pairing
passages.quote: `Breakdown.matInner`: This is the Frobenius inner product of two derivative matrices written through their coordinate columns. It supplies the weak diffusion pairing and the pinning functional ℓᵢ.

passages.title: Gradient matrix pairing
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.matInner` (1): The paper writes (∇v)ⱼₖ=∂ⱼvₖ; applying G to eⱼ produces the vector with components indexed by k, so the pairing agrees after matching these indices.

passages.title: Gradient matrix pairing
passages.quote: Clause 1 of `Breakdown.matInner`, lines 14-15: This is the Frobenius inner product of two derivative matrices written through their coordinate columns.

passages.title: Trace of the weak Hessian

passages.title: Period-averaged L² norm

passages.title: Euclidean norm of coefficients

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: `Breakdown.IsCertificate`: These are the full hypotheses for the older certificate-to-profile theorem, including analytic estimates for every admissible perturbation and finite arithmetic inequalities. They are an alternative to the final Section 7 certificate, with unit multiplier weight, direct approximate-profile coercivity, a local-ball forcing term and a slope-inverse box condition.

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsCertificate` (1): The coercive estimate is universally quantified over perturbations, multiplier vectors and measurable finite-L² right sides; it cannot be checked by testing the approximate profile alone.

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsCertificate` (2): Joint C² regularity in parameter, time and space and a second-derivative decay bound are stronger written requirements than the family conditions on p.31.

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsCertificate` (3): The positive weight, positive periods, positive coerciveTotal and positive twist guard the divisions and square roots in the scalar bounds.

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsCertificate` (4): The strict nontriviality inequality forces the profile-gradient integral to have a positive finite toReal value: both zero and infinity give zero and fail.

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsCertificate` (5): No positivity is imposed on ballRadius; an inactive local term still leaves all global, coercive, nontriviality and parameter obligations.

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsCertificate` (6): A half-period symmetry permits twist=2; twist=1 is also allowed as a conservative choice even when that symmetry exists.

passages.title: Conditions of the earlier certificate
passages.quote: Encoding for `Breakdown.IsCertificate` (7): The pin coefficient is required nonnegative here, while the paper initially lists c₂ as real; comparing the full predicates requires more than matching that sign.

passages.quote: Field `Breakdown.IsCertificate.radius_nonneg`: Every coordinate radius is nonnegative, so the parameter box contains its centre.

Breakdown.divergenceAt.text: Mathlib’s fderiv is total and is zero when differentiability fails; the smooth-solution and smooth-profile hypotheses supply differentiability where this operator is used.

Breakdown.sumSecondPartialsAt.text: The derivative expression is meaningful as the classical Laplacian under the surrounding smoothness hypotheses; it does not assert differentiability by itself.

Breakdown.gradientAt.text: The raw fderiv operation is total; smooth_pressure or the profile’s smooth-pressure clause supplies the needed regularity.

Breakdown.advectionAt.text: The operation does not carry a differentiability proof; the classical and weak interfaces provide separate regularity contracts.

Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution.text: ContDiffOn controls the initial trace and prevents a jump at time zero. For t>0 the regularity domain contains a neighbourhood, so deriv, fderiv and iteratedFDeriv are actual derivatives there.

Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace.text: The datum may depend on ν: the quantifier order is for every ν>0, there exists u₀. The energy bound C is inside the forbidden solution existential; no fixed choice of a negative C can remove legitimate solutions.

Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus.text: The torus is encoded by periodic functions on R³, rather than by a quotient type. The existential pressure may be any smooth pressure; periodicity is imposed only on u₀ and u.

Breakdown.SimilarityResidual.text: The classical derivative operations require the smoothness supplied by PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists.

Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist.text: R is a linear isometric equivalence, so its inverse is genuine; reflections are allowed. The nonzero clause is pointwise, and smoothness prevents a null-set modification of zero from satisfying it.

Breakdown.IsTestFunction.text: A test is compactly supported in space; time is absent from this predicate.

Breakdown.IsWeakGradient.text: The derivative is supplied as data and constrained by the test identity; fderiv f is not used. Mathlib’s Bochner integral is total, but local integrability and compact test support guard these particular integrals.

Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestField.text: Support is compact in the joint time-space variable; these tests are not required to be time-periodic.

Breakdown.weakSimilarityIntegrand.text: The test’s derivatives are classical; W enters without a time derivative, and G supplies its weak spatial gradient. The pressure term vanishes against the divergence-free tests.

Breakdown.WeakPeriodicSimilarityProfileE.text: The same finite real C bounds the sixth-power velocity integral and squared operator-norm gradient integral for every time. The gradient in this predicate uses the norm on continuous linear maps; the certificate’s matSq is the Frobenius square, an equivalent finite-dimensional norm.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_space.text: The profile remains an assumption; this theorem does not produce a numerical profile or validate a certificate.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus.text: The conclusion has neither an explicit blow-up time nor a rate or local convergence estimate. The theorem shown here is a stub, with the proof exposed separately by Solution.lean.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_space_of_weak.text: The weak hypothesis includes actual integrability and product-a.e. nontriviality; a pointwise spike in a zero equivalence class is excluded. This is a readable theorem stub, not a proof replay receipt.

Breakdown.Symmetry.text: The time shift is in normalized time θ; in the final profile it becomes θ₀S, as in (7.39), p.35.

Breakdown.matSq.text: The paper writes (∇v)ⱼₖ=∂ⱼvₖ; in Lean this component is (G(eⱼ))ₖ, giving the same scalar norm despite the different storage convention.

Breakdown.matInner.text: The paper writes (∇v)ⱼₖ=∂ⱼvₖ; applying G to eⱼ produces the vector with components indexed by k, so the pairing agrees after matching these indices.

Breakdown.secondDerivTrace.text: This is an algebraic trace of supplied data; IsPerturbation or IsProfileField connects H to actual weak derivatives.

Breakdown.periodLIntegral.text: ENNReal.ofReal truncates negative inputs to zero; arbitrary signed f therefore cannot be interpreted as a signed integral through this helper. The integral may be infinite, so finiteness must be supplied before using toReal.

Breakdown.periodBallLIntegral.text: The radius is not required to be positive in CertificateData or IsCertificate; a nonpositive radius gives a null spatial domain for Lebesgue integration. ENNReal.ofReal clips negative inputs, and the value can be infinite.

Breakdown.periodNorm.text: ENNReal.toReal sends infinity to zero, so this raw helper is not an L² norm on arbitrary fields. IsCertificate.coercive explicitly requires the right side’s squared integral to be finite; finite residual budgets provide the corresponding guard for residual fields.

Breakdown.periodBallNorm.text: The same toReal-infinity default as periodNorm applies to arbitrary inputs. For an admissible right side the global L² hypothesis also makes the restricted integral finite.

Breakdown.vecNorm.text: When k=0 the sum is empty and the norm is zero; the paper explicitly permits zero dimensions on p.35.

Breakdown.IsTimePeriodic.text: The recurrence is pointwise for every time and point, even when the surrounding field is used through an almost-everywhere class.

Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestVector.text: Compact support is in the joint time-space variable; there is no periodicity requirement.

Breakdown.IsPerturbation.text: The structure has no standalone hypothesis P>0; certificate period_pos supplies it before this predicate is used in the main route. Only the combined time-and-dilation derivative g is required to lie in L², as in the discussion following (7.4).

Breakdown.IsRightSide.text: This predicate alone does not assert measurability or L² finiteness of F; IsCertificate.coercive supplies them separately. The supplied g is the time-and-dilation part only; diffusion is recovered by integration by parts from G.

Breakdown.weightedEnergy.text: A bounded measurable positive weight and the perturbation’s finite derivative integrals are needed before treating the totalized real value as the intended energy. ENNReal.ofReal clips a negative density and toReal maps infinity to zero; IsCertificate’s weight and finiteness clauses prevent these defaults on admissible inputs.

Breakdown.pinValue.text: The Bochner integral is totalized; pin_finite together with gradient_finite provides the L² pairing control in certificate applications. The pin matrix need not itself be a derivative, divergence-free, or periodic in this readable predicate.

Breakdown.IsProfileField.text: The predicate is spatial and has no time variable. Its L⁶ requirement selects the homogeneous Sobolev representative and rules out nonzero constant velocities.

Breakdown.frozenForm.text: The input named w is the test velocity here, rather than the scalar weight. The signed Bochner integrals need the stationary field’s Sobolev regularity and the profile bounds in certificate applications.

Breakdown.stationaryEnergy.text: The raw signed integrals are interpreted using the positive bounded measurable weight and the L² conditions supplied by the certificate and IsProfileField.

Breakdown.defectField.text: The paper allows any residual representative modulo gradients; this earlier interface chooses one using a C¹ pressure. Division by zero is total in Lean, so period_pos is needed before reading 1/P as the intended time scaling.

Breakdown.supBoundFactor.text: Real.sqrt and division are total operations; the certificate’s weight_pos supplies w_*>0 and makes the intended constant positive.

Breakdown.CertificateData.text: The record contains data only; none of its signs, bounds or regularity claims holds until IsCertificate is supplied. The multiplier weight is fixed to one in this interface, and coercivity is assumed directly at the approximate profile.

Breakdown.CertificateData.box.text: Order on Fin k → R is pointwise, so Set.Icc means simultaneous coordinate bounds. radius_nonneg ensures that the centre belongs to the box; zero radii and k=0 remain allowed.

Breakdown.IsCertificate.text: The coercive estimate is universally quantified over perturbations, multiplier vectors and measurable finite-L² right sides; it cannot be checked by testing the approximate profile alone. Joint C² regularity in parameter, time and space and a second-derivative decay bound are stronger written requirements than the family conditions on p.31.

Breakdown.CertificateHypothesis.text: The existential does not restrict k to be positive; empty multiplier families remain possible and all remaining analytic conditions still apply. No concrete numerical certificate is constructed by this definition.

Breakdown.certificate_orbit.text: This readable theorem is a proof stub; Solution.lean invokes certificate_orbit_proved in the library. The output does not state smoothness, identity isometry, the original Γ symmetries or a same-witness error bound.

Breakdown.CoerciveClause.text: The quantifiers cover every parameter in the box, every admissible perturbation, every coefficient vector and every measurable periodic L² right-hand side satisfying the weak equation. This ball L² estimate is an earlier formulation, not a literal substitution of finitely many rows in (7.17).

Breakdown.periodPairing.text: Mathlib real Bochner integrals are total and equal zero on nonintegrable inputs. periodPairing_abs_le establishes integrability under its explicit L² hypotheses.

Breakdown.MultiplierInequality.text: The existential multiplier and frequency norm occur after the perturbation, coefficients and right-hand side; one universal multiplier for all inputs is not required. The K term measures F on a ball and the force coefficient weight is one; these differ from the extended certificate used in the printed paper.

Breakdown.periodPairing_abs_le.text: Both finite ENNReal square integrals and both almost-everywhere measurability assumptions are needed for this interpretation. The source proof establishes integrability before applying the product-integral and L² inequalities.

Breakdown.coercive_scalar_core.text: The hypothesis c > 0 rules out totalized division by zero and makes √c positive. E and S encode the field energy and squared coefficient norm, while the retained frequency term has nonnegative coefficient cμ.

Breakdown.coerciveClause_of_multiplierIn.text: The comparison hypotheses may enlarge the resulting constants because all norms multiplying them are nonnegative. Integrability of the pairing is supplied by periodPairing_abs_le, rather than assumed from the bare definition.

Breakdown.axialRot.text: Fin 3 uses coordinates 0, 1 and 2; the paper’s y₃ axis is coordinate 2.

Breakdown.modeAverage.text: The real time interval has length one; the angle interval has length 2π. The complex interval integrals are total Bochner integrals; analytic callers establish the needed integrability.

Breakdown.modeVel.text: Use (n,k) = (2ι₂−ι₁, κι₁) when comparing this generic mode with the paper’s Eι. The components are complex Fourier coefficients even though v is a real vector field.

Breakdown.modeGrad.text: The second index is the direction supplied to the continuous linear map G; the first is the resulting vector component. A pointwise arbitrary G need not be the gradient of v; IsPerturbation supplies the weak-gradient identity.

Breakdown.modeSecondDeriv.text: The tensor is supplied as H, with weak-derivative compatibility imposed by IsPerturbation. The component norm used later is a finite sum of squared complex components, not the operator norm of H.

Breakdown.cnormSq.text: For a matrix or tensor this is the componentwise Frobenius norm; the conversion-weight Hessians use a different operator norm. The sum over an empty index type is zero; the active velocity and derivative arrays use nonempty Fin 3 products.

Breakdown.curlOfGrad.text: The array entry g(l,j) represents ∂j v_l; transposing the array without changing this contraction reverses its interpretation.

Breakdown.curlGradOfSecondDeriv.text: Weak derivative compatibility and symmetry of second derivatives are analytic facts supplied by the perturbation hypotheses, not by this algebraic contraction.

Breakdown.cylRadius.text: The square-root argument is a sum of squares, so it is nonnegative. r is zero on the axis; the gain theorem is an almost-everywhere statement and the axis is a null set.

Breakdown.IsAxisymmetric.text: The invariance is pointwise for every angle and point, rather than merely almost everywhere.

Breakdown.shiftedFrequency.text: Division is total in Lean; the relevant admissibility predicate separately requires P > 0. The paper’s κ is a spatial harmonic scale, while the generic second frequency coordinate here is already k = κι₁.

Breakdown.meanField.text: Taking real parts returns a real vector field; mean-mode invariance is proved elsewhere. Evaluation at time zero is part of the mode reconstruction and does not restrict the original profile to its initial value.

Breakdown.curlVec.text: The expression is algebraic for any G; calling it the curl of a field requires G to be that field’s derivative.

Breakdown.vortGrad.text: DDW is an iterated continuous-linear-map representation of the Hessian; the tensor contraction assumes its derivative meaning at analytic call sites.

Breakdown.stretchForm.text: fderiv is total and returns a default derivative at points of nondifferentiability; the strong multiplier theorems require W to be C². The weak certificate route replaces the second derivative calls by a separately supplied weak Hessian in ExtendedCoerciveChallenge.

Breakdown.FlowBounds.text: The structure stores real numbers and functions without asserting they are valid bounds; FlowBounds.IsValid supplies those inequalities.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.text: The raw structure imposes no finiteness, symmetry, sign, decay or denominator condition; ModeWeights.IsAdmissible supplies them. The presence of classOf gives C an inhabitant even though Finite C alone would permit an empty type.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.eps.text: The signed weight still occurs in the multiplier pairing; replacing it there by its magnitude would lose the Fourier sign.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.mu.text: Its nonnegativity follows from the absolute value even before admissibility is imposed.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.dop.text: Positive P is a separate admissibility field; the raw function remains defined at P = 0.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.epsGrad.text: The weights are Lipschitz under admissibility, so their derivatives are meaningful almost everywhere even when they have spline knots. The total fderiv value at a nondifferentiable point does not assert differentiability there.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.muGrad.text: The derivative is used under the Lipschitz and decay conditions of ModeWeights.IsAdmissible; it is a total function outside those conditions.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.epsNb.text: The supremum is a finite supremum in nonnegative reals and is zero when the wave set is empty. It is not a conditionally complete real supremum over an unbounded set.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.muNb.text: The finite nonnegative supremum returns zero for an empty wave set, representing absence of those wave couplings.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.ind.text: Classical decidability is used for arbitrary propositions; the definition is mathematical and need not be an executable membership test.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.shareHat.text: The first share is active if the weight or its derivative is nonzero; the second is active if a neighbouring weight is positive. Admissibility requires D to lie below the remaining share.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.secondDerivNorm.text: This norm is an operator norm, unlike the Frobenius norms used for the Fourier derivative arrays. The conversion weights are required to be C² before their Hessian norms are used analytically.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.coefA.text: All denominator guards come from ModeWeights.IsAdmissible, with share1 required positive where the curl weight or its gradient is active. The whole formula belongs to the earlier class-weight route and should not be presented as the paper’s displayed piecewise formula.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.coefAA.text: The coefficient may have either sign; pointwise positivity of the full density is a separate obligation.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.penalty.text: The existence tests are global in space; a locally zero weight can still activate a global-support penalty. The eta and etaMin denominators are strictly positive under admissibility.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.coefB.text: The coefficient need not be nonnegative by definition; later lower-bound arguments handle negative terms.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.coefC.text: The mixed term has an overall negative sign when modeDensity is assembled; its sign cannot be inferred from this name alone.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.modeDensity.text: The input order is x2 = |∇²v̂|, xc = |∇curl v̂|, x1 = |∇v̂|, xo = |curl v̂| and x0 = |v̂|. The displayed raw algebra does not assert any amplitude is nonnegative or comes from a field.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.modeTerm.text: The square roots of the finite sums of squared moduli are nonnegative. The weak derivative relations between v, G and H are supplied by IsPerturbation.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.frequencySeminormS.text: The ENNReal sum and nonnegative integral may take the value infinity; they do not silently default to zero. multiplier_density explicitly proves finiteness before this quantity is used as a real norm.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.IsAdmissible.text: Derivative bounds use total fderiv, while global Lipschitz conditions supply almost-everywhere differentiability. share1 may vanish only where both the curl weight and its derivative are inactive; every other displayed denominator has a separate strict-positivity guard.

Breakdown.gradField.text: At an arbitrary nonsmooth input, fderiv is a total operation and must not be read as a proof of differentiability.

Breakdown.secondDerivField.text: The nested fderiv calls are total outside the regularity hypotheses and do not themselves certify a Hessian.

Breakdown.symPartForm.text: No symmetric matrix is constructed: the antisymmetric part contributes zero to this scalar quadratic form.

Breakdown.FlowBounds.IsValid.text: A numerical table of majorants alone is insufficient; this predicate binds each bound to W. The harmonic reconstruction is pointwise for all times and spatial points.

Breakdown.IsPeriodicTestField.text: The support radius is chosen before all times and points, giving one radius uniform in time. The divergence constraint is pointwise because the test field is smooth.

Breakdown.IsPeriodicTestPotential.text: The predicate is an encoding of the divergence-free requirement on M, not an additional pressure field for the perturbation. The support radius is uniform in time.

Breakdown.cdot.text: This pairing is not the unconjugated complex bilinear dot product.

Breakdown.cdotMat.text: The Frobenius pairing conjugates the second matrix componentwise.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.IsMultiplierField.text: The real Fourier series in the final identity is a total tsum, whose raw value need not represent a convergent series for arbitrary inputs. For admissible callers, Breakdown/Cert/CoerciveField.lean:495-514 supplies fieldModeTerm_summable; the raw definition does not carry this proof.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.densityPos.text: Each term is clipped separately by ENNReal.ofReal, before summation; this is not the positive part of a pre-summed signed series. The value may be infinity, and no real conversion is made here.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.densityNeg.text: The ENNReal sum retains infinite negative mass as infinity. Finite negative mass is required by the assembly theorem; it cannot be removed by a later toReal call.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.multiplierConstant.text: Positive c, cμ and w₀ are separate admissibility fields; the raw formula is total at zero denominators. epsSup, epsGradSup and ratio correspond to nλ, n∇λ and nμ for the appropriate weight encoding.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.multiplierGap.text: The frequency seminorm uses ENNReal.toReal; multiplier_density separately supplies its finiteness. The definition alone does not assert that the real converted energy is the intended finite integral.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.multiplier_density.text: This source file contains a proof stub; the implementation is re-exported from Solution.lean using multiplier_density_proved. The hypothesis W ∈ C² guards all classical derivatives; the active weak-Hessian route is a separate extension.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.azimuthalDensity_n.text: The inequalities relating x0, x1 and x2 are hypotheses; the theorem does not derive them from Fourier symmetry. The quotients are total at r = 0, but the analytic use of angular gains is almost everywhere away from the rotation axis.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.mode_azimuthal_gai.text: The statement holds almost everywhere in space-time, so the zero cylindrical radius is confined to a null exceptional set. Only two of the four inequalities displayed in (B.35) are included in this export.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.stretchCharge.text: The coefficient √2 + 1/2 belongs to this earlier bound; the printed cell argument uses its own sharper constants and a different bound decomposition. Its denominator len is guarded by a strict-positivity assumption in stretch_mean_bound.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.stretch_mean_bound.text: The left side is ENNReal.ofReal of the negative mean, so a nonnegative mean contributes zero. The conclusion is almost everywhere in space, and the right side is a nonnegative extended-real series.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.le_of_ennreal_boun.text: The finite-Dn assumption is essential: with Dp = Dn = ∞, both premises hold for X = 0 and Y = 1, but the real conclusion fails. The proof establishes Dp < ∞ before converting either extended-real mass to a real number.

Breakdown.ModeWeights.multiplierInequali.text: The rest hypothesis is required for every compatible multiplier, so the multiplier obtained from the existence theorem can be used without a new choice. Finiteness of the negative density is part of the rest hypothesis and is passed to le_of_ennreal_bounds.

Breakdown.EpsPiece.text: modes is an arbitrary mathematical Set and can be infinite. The raw structure does not exclude overlap with its negative; the positive one-sided frequency condition later enforces disjointness.

Breakdown.MuPiece.text: The mode set can be infinite even though the number of pieces is finite. Zero piece counts are allowed by Fin nM; all remaining certificate requirements still have to hold.

Breakdown.HarmonicBounds.text: These fields are proposed bounds until the associated admissibility inequalities bind them to the actual reference field. Mode arrays use componentwise norms; supGradVort bounds the operator norm of the real derivative map.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.text: The piece families are finite, while each piece’s mode set can be infinite. The raw structure is data only; PieceWeights.IsAdmissible carries the conditions.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.sgn.text: For an arbitrary overlapping set the positive branch wins, so oddness is not a property of the raw definition alone. Membership in an infinite Set is a mathematical predicate and need not have a finite executable decision procedure.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.inPiece.text: It records support without the sign; the signed multiplier itself uses sgn.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.fwdSum.text: The sum is over the finite reference harmonic list, even if Np is infinite. The bounds are indexed by the shifting reference harmonic, not by the destination perturbation mode.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.backSum.text: Whether the current mode is in Np is checked by the caller inward; backSum by itself does not impose membership.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.inward.text: The first membership branch has priority for a malformed overlapping set; one-sided admissibility eliminates that overlap.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.outward.text: The positive and negative representatives are tested separately, so both can contribute when neither lies in Np.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.harmonicSum.text: The finite list includes the zero mode under admissibility, unlike ModeWeights.waves in the earlier mean/wave route.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.frameFreq.text: The frame rate is a real scalar for a fixed piece and parameter; it has no spatial argument. P > 0 is required by admissibility, although the raw expression is total at P = 0.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.wtGrad.text: Admissible piece weights are Lipschitz, giving ordinary derivatives almost everywhere. The total fderiv value at spline knots is not a smoothness assertion and does not replace the Lipschitz hypothesis.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.shareHat.text: The share1 indicator sees both a nonzero weight and a nonzero derivative; the outward share sees a positive weight. The denominator scale is strictly positive in the piece admissibility conditions.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.coefA.text: The formula is summed over all pieces, so overlapping pieces contribute additively even though each individual one-sided set is disjoint from its negative. Strict positivity of share1, share2, len, t0, t1, t2, t3 and scale comes from admissibility.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.coefAA.text: The Hessian norm is the operator norm of the scalar conversion weight, not the component norm of the perturbation Hessian.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.coefB.text: Each eta is strictly positive under admissibility. No sign is asserted by the definition; lower bounds for this coefficient belong to the later analytic and cell conditions.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.modeDensity.text: The amplitude order is Hessian, gradient of curl, gradient, curl and velocity. The conversion-weight conditions guarantee nonnegativity of I′₂, while the other coefficients still require the later lower-bound analysis.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.modeTerm.text: The square roots of finite sums of squared complex moduli give nonnegative amplitudes. IsPerturbation, rather than this substitution, states that G and H are the weak derivatives of v.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.seminormSq.text: ENNReal.ofReal clips negative raw inputs, so the condition that each µp is nonnegative is part of the intended interpretation. The extended-real value may be infinity; piece_multiplier_density proves it finite for admissible perturbations before real conversion.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.IsMultiplierField.text: The final sum over all modes is a real tsum; its interpretation needs the summability supplied for admissible callers. The summability witness is pieceIntegral_summable in Breakdown/Cert/CoercivePieceField.lean:830-853.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.densityPos.text: Positive parts are taken term by term before summation. This definition does not form a potentially undefined difference of two infinite signed sums.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.densityNeg.text: The value infinity remains visible in the nonnegative extended-real integral. It is not sufficient to write the formal difference of the positive and negative densities without a finite-negative-mass proof.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.multiplierGap.text: The conversion of the frequency seminorm to a real number is justified by the finiteness conclusion of the multiplier theorem. The same multiplier is used in every pairing, which matters when the forcing-field terms cancel.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.IsAdmissible.text: The frequency lower bound is chosen for each piece before quantifying over every mode in that piece; a merely pointwise positive frequency would be weaker. Because the frame frequency changes sign under mode negation, the one-sided conditions imply that Np and −Np are disjoint and exclude the zero mode.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.piece_multiplier_.text: The file contains a statement stub here; Solution.lean re-exports a proved implementation. The active certificate has a weak second derivative and uses the extension in ExtendedCoerciveChallenge rather than this C² version alone.

Breakdown.PieceWeights.multiplierInequal.text: The remainder-density hypothesis includes finite negative mass and is uniform over every compatible multiplier. The proof chooses one multiplier from piece_multiplier_density and uses exactly that multiplier in the supplied remainder bound.

Breakdown.rowNorm.text: The raw square root does not enforce nonnegative row weights or integrable pairings; IsExtendedCertificate supplies rowWeight_nonneg and finite L² rows.

Breakdown.weakDefectField.text: The time derivative and first spatial derivative are total Lean operations; the C¹ profile hypothesis supplies their intended meanings. Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params.text: Fin 0 → ℝ has one element, so a zero parameter dimension does not make the certificate conditions vacuous. The raw set uses the square of stiffRadius; the certificate separately records its nonnegative sign and the nonzero scales.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.defect.text: No continuity of the H-valued residual in the parameter is assumed here; the certificate only bounds it parameter by parameter.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.target.text: Do not identify target itself with ℓ̄; the derivative pairing must be subtracted.
